target_customer: Teachers, schools and individuals who want to collect and share content on a visual board; paid by school and teacher subscriptions
problem: Documents and slide decks are tedious to make and read; people wanted a simple collaborative canvas to post notes, links and media.
business_model: freemium SaaS with paid teacher, school and district subscriptions

founders.name: Nitesh Goel
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; Wikipedia says he started Wallwisher in 2008 with a friend from India.

founders.name: Pranav Piyush
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by Wikipedia; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: Stixy
competitors.what: Free online bulletin boards of notes, photos and files

technical_complexity.rationale: A simple real time board with posts; scaling and moderation were the later challenges.

defensibility.rationale: Similar tools existed, and teachers' accumulated boards and habits gave modest lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Google Docs and later tools overlap, but Padlet remained independent; no acquisition found.

market_need_then: Teachers used Wallwisher for classroom boards by 2009 to 2011 per education blogs, showing demand before the YC batch.

branding.name_origin: Wallwisher became Padlet; a third party commentary says each board is called a padlet, but no company statement was found.
branding.domain_note: Uses padlet.com and the short link domain padl.et; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: irreverent and funny, per the YC description

rebrands.why: Date per Wikipedia and a third party commentary; the reason is not company sourced.

branding.community_and_virality: Used by millions of students as a first creation experience, per the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Became a widely used generic term in classrooms and a product led growth engine.

outcome_analysis: Padlet grew from the Wallwisher classroom wall into a staple of teaching, reaching about 3 million monthly uniques by 2015 and over ten million users later. It raised a small seed in 2015 and later Series A money, stayed independent, and survived backlash over a 2018 move to paid pricing. Product led growth through teachers drove it.
notes: TechCrunch says about $450,000 was raised earlier from angels and YC combined, undated, so not recorded as a round. An April 2019 $11M Series A appears only on Seedtable (aggregator) and Wikipedia says over $13M across three Series A rounds as of 2020-11; both unverified so not recorded. Totals vary from $1.69M to $13M across aggregators. Padlet's page lists only one founder; Pranav Piyush comes from Wikipedia. Education and prior employers not found.
